title: Conditional Unique Games Hardness
statement: Let a family of encoded regular Unique Games, a source binary promise problem, and a finite allowed family of sign predicates be given. Suppose a tester uses only allowed predicates, has completeness at least $\beta$ on every dictator, and accepts every function with no $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$-notable coordinate with probability at most $\alpha+\operatorname{error}(\varepsilon)$; assume $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$, the error takes values in $[0,1]$ on $[0,1]$ and tends to zero as $\varepsilon$ tends to zero through positive values. Let $q>0$, and suppose the family has an optimization encoding and a Unique Games gap reduction from the source promise problem, with thresholds $s_{UG}<c_{UG}$. Suppose a finite long-code transformation for this tester has $M>0$ clones, $r\le M$, and the required arity bounds; suppose also that its output has an encoding and a polynomial-time machine implementing that encoding on canonical inputs. For real target thresholds $s_T<c_T$ and parameters $\delta_{UG},\varepsilon,\tau$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, assume $1-\delta_{UG}\le c_{UG}$, $s_{UG}<\tau\varepsilon^5/18$, $c_T\le\beta-r\delta_{UG}-r^2/M$, and $\alpha+\operatorname{error}(\varepsilon)+\tau+r^2/M\le s_T$. Then the source promise problem is polynomial-time Karp reducible to the target encoded maximization problem's gap promise with soundness threshold $s_T$ and completeness threshold $c_T$.
